# ngrrram

ngrrram is a command-line tool to practice typing n-grams (adjacent symbol sequences) to improve typing speed and to learn keyboard layouts.

A short showcase of the UI is available in the repository's assets.

Installation

- Precompiled releases are available for common platforms.
- Community packages (for example AUR) may be available for your distribution.

Usage

ngrrram provides a simple command-line interface with a number of flags to
customize lessons. Typical usage:

Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>    your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>   the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho         show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb               pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat                the most important flag. don\'t practice alone.
  -h, --help               Print help

Default recommended invocation:

  ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100

Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout you must specify both the input layout
(--emu-in) and the output layout (--emu-out). Supported layouts include:

- qwerty, qwertz, azerty, dvorak, colemak, colemakdh

Notes

- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of that lesson.
- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.

# ngrrram

`ngrrram` is a CLI tool to practice typing ngrams (`n` adjacent symbols in
particular order) to improve your typing speed and/or learn new keyboard
layouts effectively.

![a showcase of the ngrrram ui](./.github/showcase.gif)

Certain letter combination occur a lot more often than others, thus practicing
these in particular makes sense. This type of practice is often recommended for
example by [Ben Vallack](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sI-a64EVPPU) and Josh
Kaufman, who [learned Colemak in just 20 hours](https://first20hours.com)
making strong use of ngrams.

There already exists a good tool for this type of practice called
[ngram-type](https://github.com/ranelpadon/ngram-type). This tool is *heavily*
inspired by `ngram-type` and I want to thank Ranel Padon for creating it.

However, ngram-type does not support emulating different keyboard layouts,
which I found important so I would not have to switch my whole system to a
layout I was still learning.

Also, some people might prefer local/offline CLI based solutions over web based
ones.

## Installation

### Releases

Precompiled [releases](https://github.com/wintermute-cell/ngrrram/releases) for
linux, windows and macos are available.

### AUR (maintained by [JinEnMok](https://github.com/JinEnMok))

Use `yay` or any other AUR helper to install for an Archlinux system:

```bash
yay -S ngrrram-git
or
yay -S ngrrram-bin
```

### From Source

Make sure you have the rust tooling installed, then simply run:

```bash
cargo build --release
```

The executable will then be located at `./target/release/ngrrram`

### Looking for help packaging!

If you'd like to help by packaging for your platform, I'd gladly accept!

## Usage

`ngrrram` is not very complex. It offers a few customization options as command
flags, but starts with the recommended defaults if unconfigured.

Options:
```
Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]

      --emu-out <layout>  the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layout

# ngrrram

ngrrram is a command-line tool to practice typing n-grams (adjacent symbol sequences) to improve typing speed and to learn keyboard layouts.

A short showcase of the UI is available in the repository's assets.

Installation

- Precompiled releases are available for common platforms.
- Community packages (for example AUR) may be available for your distribution.

Usage

ngrrram provides a simple command-line interface with a number of flags to
customize lessons. Typical usage:

Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>    your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>   the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho         show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb               pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat                the most important flag. don\'t practice alone.
  -h, --help               Print help

Default recommended invocation:

  ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100

Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout you must specify both the input layout
(--emu-in) and the output layout (--emu-out). Supported layouts include:

- qwerty, qwertz, azerty, dvorak, colemak, colemakdh

Notes

- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of that lesson.
- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.

</output>

<output>
# ngrrram

`ngrrram` is a CLI tool to practice typing ngrams (`n` adjacent symbols in
particular order) to improve your typing speed and/or learn new keyboard
layouts effectively.

![a showcase of the ngrrram ui](./.github/showcase.gif)

Certain letter combination occur a lot more often than others, thus practicing
these in particular makes sense. This type of practice is often recommended for
example by [Ben Vallack](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sI-a64EVPPU) and Josh
Kaufman, who [learned Colemak in just 20 hours](https://first20hours.com)
making strong use of ngrams.

There already exists a good tool for this type of practice called
[ngram-type](https://github.com/ranelpadon/ngram-type). This tool is *heavily*
inspired by `ngram-type` and I want to thank Ranel Padon for creating it.

However, ngram-type does not support emulating different keyboard layouts,
which I found important so I would not have to switch my whole system to a
layout I was still learning.

Also, some people might prefer local/offline CLI based solutions over web based
ones.

## Installation

### Releases

Precompiled [releases](https://github.com/wintermute-cell/ngrrram/releases) for
linux, windows and macos are available.

### AUR (maintained by [JinEnMok](https://github.com/JinEnMok))

Use `yay` or any other AUR helper to install for an Archlinux system:

```bash
yay -S ngrrram-git
or
yay -S ngrrram-bin
```

### From Source

Make sure you have the rust tooling installed, then simply run:

```bash
cargo build --release
```

The executable will then be located at `./target/release/ngrrram`

### Looking for help packaging!

If you'd like to help by packaging for your platform, I'd gladly accept!

## Usage

`ngrrram` is not very complex. It offers a few customization options as command
flags, but starts with the recommended defaults if unconfigured.

Options:
```
Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>   your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>  the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho        show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb              pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat               the most important flag. don't practice alone.
  -h, --help              Print help
```

If you start `ngrrram` without parameters, it uses these recommended defaults:
```bash
ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100
```

## Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout in `ngrrram`, you must pass the flags
`--emu-in` and `--emu-out`, the first one describing your current layout, and
the second one being the one you want to emulate.

Available layouts are:

- `qwerty`    (Qwerty)
- `qwertz`    (Qwertz)
- `azerty`    (Azerty)
- `dvorak`    (Dvorak)
- `colemak`   (Colemak)
- `colemakdh` (ColemakDH)

> Having to provide an input layout is sub-optimal. I'm not sure how to get
> layout independent scancodes in rust; Could not get `device_query` to work.
> If you know a solution, please tell me.

## Random Notes
- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of
  that lesson; no need to stress.
- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.
  Otherwise WPM would unnaturally skyrocket with smaller ngrams.
</output>

out=run("tmux capture-pane -t test -p -e")

print(out.stdout)
PY

"}

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from probe import Sess
for args in ["", "--show-ortho","--nokb"]:
    s=Sess("test",args,80,24)
    lines=s.cap().splitlines()
    print("ARGS",args)
    for i,l in enumerate(lines[:19]):
        inner=l[1:-1] if len(l)>=2 and l[0]=='│' else l
        # find first non-space in inner
        idx=None
        for j,c in enumerate(inner):
            if c!=' ':
                idx=j; break
        print(i, "inner first",idx, "inner len",len(inner), "find ngrrram",inner.find("ngrrram"), "find Lesson",inner.find("Lesson"), "find check",inner.find("✔"), "find keyboard top",inner.find("┌"), "find q",inner.find("q"), repr(inner[:60]))
    s.kill()
PY
python3 /tmp/coords2.py

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from probe import Sess, run
import time
keys=["Enter","Tab","BSpace","DC","Up","Down","Left","Right","Home","End","C-x","C-a","C-z","F1","PageDown","Space","BTab"]
# DC is delete? tmux names: DC
for key in keys:
    s=Sess("test","--nokb -c 1 -r 1",80,24)
    lesson=s.cap().splitlines()[6].strip().strip('│').strip()
    orig=s.cap()
    try:
        run(f"tmux send-keys -t test {key}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(key, e)
    time.sleep(0.4)
    after=s.cap()
    changed = (orig!=after)
    print(f"{key}: changed={changed}")
    if changed:
        # print rows 6,7
        print("  row6", after.splitlines()[6])
        print("  row7", after.splitlines()[7])
        print("  row3", after.splitlines()[3])
    s.kill()
PY
python3 /tmp/keys.py 2>&1 | head -n 200

    return 'x' if ch!='x' else 'z'
def trial(desc, make_seq):
    # make_seq(lesson) returns list of ops: strings to send -l, or "BSpace", "Space"
    s=Sess("test","--nokb -c 1 -r 1",80,24)
    les=s.cap().splitlines()[6][1:-1].strip()
    seq=make_seq(les)
    for op in seq:
        if op=="BSpace":
            s.keys("BSpace",delay=0.15)
        elif op=="Space":
            s.keys("Space",delay=0.15)
        else:
            run(f"tmux send-keys -t test -l {shlex.quote(op)}"); time.sleep(0.25)
    time.sleep(0.4)
    lines=s.cap().splitlines()
    print(f"{desc:45} les={les!r} seq={seq} -> row3={lines[3].strip()!r} wpm={lines[10].strip()!r} acc={lines[11].strip()!r} row6={lines[6].strip()!r}")
    s.kill()

trial("perfect", lambda l: [l+" "])
trial("1 wrong first, rest ok", lambda l: [wrong_for(l[0])+l[1]+" "])
trial("1 wrong second, rest ok", lambda l: [l[0]+wrong_for(l[1])+" "])
trial("2 wrong, space ok", lambda l: [wrong_for(l[0])+wrong_for(l[1])+" "])
trial("wrong2nd, bspace, correct", lambda l: [l[0]+wrong_for(l[1]), "BSpace", l[1]+" "])
trial("wrong1st, bspace, perfect", lambda l: [wrong_for(l[0]), "BSpace", l+" "])
trial("wrong space pos, bspace, space", lambda l: [l+wrong_for(' '), "BSpace", "Space"])
trial("wrong,bs,wrong,bs,perfect", lambda l: [wrong_for(l[0]),"BSpace",wrong_for(l[0]),"BSpace",l+" "])
trial("bspace empty, perfect", lambda l: ["BSpace", l+" "])
trial("correct1, bspace, perfect", lambda l: [l[0],"BSpace",l+" "])
trial("perfect but extra bspace before final space", lambda l: [l,"BSpace",l[1]+" "]) # careful: typing l (2) then bspace removes 2nd, then l[1] then space
trial("all wrong then space? (x x space) acc", lambda l: ["xx "])
PY
python3 /tmp/acc.py 2>&1
"}

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from probe import Sess, run
import time
chars=[chr(i) for i in range(32,127)]

s.kill()

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from probe import Sess, run
import time, shlex, collections, json
def sample(args, combi, lessons, outfile):
    s=Sess("test",args,80,24)
    cnt=collections.Counter()
    total_lessons=0
    for i in range(lessons):
        les=s.cap().splitlines()[6][1:-1].strip()
        toks=les.split()
        # only count if number tokens equals combi * rep? rep=1 so == combi and lesson fits (len les+? ) if les length >=77 truncation risk; skip counting last lesson if row full?

    print(args, "distinct", len(cnt), "total tokens counted", sum(cnt.values()))
    print(sorted(cnt.items()))
    json.dump(dict(cnt), open(outfile,'w'))

import pty, os, sys, time, select, signal
# run in workspace
pid, fd = pty.fork()
if pid==0:
    os.chdir("/workspace")
    os.execv("/workspace/executable", ["./executable","--nokb","-c","1","-r","1"])
else:
    # set winsize
    import fcntl, termios, struct
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH",24,80,0,0))
    data=b""
    time.sleep(1.0)
    while True:
        r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.2)
        if not r: break
        try: chunk=os.read(fd,65536)
        except OSError: break
        if not chunk: break
        data+=chunk
    print("initial bytes len",len(data))
    print(repr(data[:4000]))
    # send a char 'x' (wrong maybe)
    os.write(fd,b"x")
    time.sleep(0.5)
    data2=b""
    while True:
        r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.2)
        if not r: break
        try: chunk=os.read(fd,65536)
        except: break
        if not chunk: break
        data2+=chunk
    print("after x len",len(data2), repr(data2[:4000]))
    # esc
    os.write(fd,b"\x1b")
    time.sleep(0.5)
    data3=b""
    while True:
        r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.2)
        if not r: break
        try: chunk=os.read(fd,65536)
        except: break
        if not chunk: break
        data3+=chunk
    print("after esc len",len(data3), repr(data3[:4000]))
    # wait exit
    try:
        wp, status = os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
        print("wait",wp,status, "exitcode", os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status) if wp else None)

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from probe import Sess, run
import time, re, os, shlex
def get_lesson_span(s):
    line=s.cap(True).splitlines()[6]
    # find [1m ... [0m
    m=re.search(r'\x1b\[1m(.*?)\x1b\[0m', line)
    return m.group(1) if m else None
def collect_file(path, top=50, combi=3, nlessons=20):
    s=Sess("test", f"--nokb -n {path} -t {top} -c {combi} -r 1",80,24)
    seen=[]
    for i in range(nlessons):
        les=get_lesson_span(s)
        seen.append(les)
        if les is None or les=="": break
        # attempt complete: type exact les (it already includes trailing spaces? span includes trailing space of lesson as built) - if span is lesson string, typing it should complete if it ends space. But if token has trailing.. just type les

        # detect lesson # unchanged? we'll just continue; next capture may same
    s.kill()
    uniq=[]
    for x in seen:

    while time.time()<end:

        if r:
            try: chunk=os.read(master,65536)
            except OSError: break
            if not chunk: break
            data+=chunk; end=time.time()+0.2

os.write(master,b"\x1b"); data=read_all(0.8); print("after esc",len(data), repr(data[:2000]))

import os, pty, subprocess, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct, sys, re
def run_and_capture(args, duration=1.2):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    def preexec():
        os.setsid(); fcntl.ioctl(1, termios.TIOCSCTTY, 0); fcntl.ioctl(1, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH",24,80,0,0))
    p=subprocess.Popen(["/workspace/executable"]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, cwd="/workspace", close_fds=True, preexec_fn=preexec)
    os.close(slave); os.set_blocking(master, False)
    start=time.time(); data=b""
    while time.time()-start<duration:
        r,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],0.05)
        if r:
            try: d=os.read(master,65536)
            except: break
            if d: data+=d
    p.kill(); 
    try: os.close(master)
    except: pass
    # find all cursor moves before ?25h
    moves=re.findall(rb'\x1b\[(\d+);(\d+)H\x1b\[39m\x1b\[49m\x1b\[59m\x1b\[0m\x1b\[\?25h', data)
    # also generic last moves
    last=data[-2000:]
    return moves[-5:], last
for combi in [1,6,25,26,27,28,30]:
    moves,last=run_and_capture(["--nokb","-c",str(combi),"-r","1"])
    print("combi",combi,"L",3*combi,"moves (row,col) last",moves)

def xf(c): return 'x' if c!='x' else 'z'

def do_lesson(kind):

        run(f"tmux send-keys -t test -l {shlex.quote(xf(les[0]))}"); time.sleep(0.08); s.keys("BSpace",delay=0.08)
    elif kind=="85": # 6/7: 1 wrong cycle, perfect
        run(f"tmux send-keys -t test -l {shlex.quote(xf(les[0]))}"); time.sleep(0.08); s.keys("BSpace",delay=0.08)
    elif kind=="86": # 13/15: 6 correct repeat cycles, 2 wrong cycles, perfect : num core (perfect5+2 wrongcorr=7?) Wait compute: correct cycles add 6 each 1/1, wrong cycles each adds correct via B (1) and total2, perfect inserts 5 correct. Num=6+2+5=13 Den=6+4+5=15
        for i in range(6):
            run(f"tmux send-keys -t test -l {shlex.quote(les[0])}"); time.sleep(0.08); s.keys("BSpace",delay=0.08)
        for i in range(2):
            run(f"tmux send-keys -t test -l {shlex.quote(xf(les[0]))}"); time.sleep(0.08); s.keys("BSpace",delay=0.08)
    run(f"tmux send-keys -t test -l {shlex.quote(les+' ')}"); time.sleep(0.35)
    lines=s.cap().splitlines(); print(kind, les, lines[11].strip())
for k in ["90","85","86"]:
    do_lesson(k)
s.kill()

#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "usage"), allow(dead_code))]
use std::borrow::Cow;

/// Terminal-styling container
///
/// Styling may be encoded as [ANSI Escape Code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code)
///
/// # Examples
///
/// ```rust
/// # use clap_builder as clap;
/// // `cstr!` converts tags to ANSI codes
/// let after_help: &'static str = color_print::cstr!(
/// r#"<bold><underline>Examples</underline></bold>
///
///   <dim>$</dim> <bold>mybin --input file.toml</bold>
/// "#);
///
/// let cmd = clap::Command::new("mybin")
///     .after_help(after_help)  // The `&str` gets converted into a `StyledStr`
///     // ...
/// #   ;
/// ```
#[derive(Clone, Default, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct StyledStr(String);

impl StyledStr {
    /// Create an empty buffer
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self(String::new())
    }

    /// Display using [ANSI Escape Code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code) styling
    #[cfg(feature = "color")]
    pub fn ansi(&self) -> impl std::fmt::Display + '_ {
        self.0.as_str()
    }

    /// May allow the compiler to consolidate the `Drop`s for `msg`, reducing code size compared to
    /// `styled.push_str(&msg)`
    pub(crate) fn push_string(&mut self, msg: String) {
        self.0.push_str(&msg);
    }

    /// Appends a given string slice onto the end of this `StyledStr`.
    pub fn push_str(&mut self, msg: &str) {
        self.0.push_str(msg);
    }

    pub(crate) fn trim_start_lines(&mut self) {
        if let Some(pos) = self.0.find('\n') {
            let (leading, help) = self.0.split_at(pos + 1);
            if leading.trim().is_empty() {
                self.0 = help.to_owned();
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn trim_end(&mut self) {
        self.0 = self.0.trim_end().to_owned();
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "help")]
    pub(crate) fn replace_newline_var(&mut self) {
        self.0 = self.0.replace("{n}", "\n");
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "help")]
    pub(crate) fn indent(&mut self, initial: &str, trailing: &str) {
        self.0.insert_str(0, initial);

        let mut line_sep = "\n".to_owned();
        line_sep.push_str(trailing);
        self.0 = self.0.replace('\n', &line_sep);
    }

    #[cfg(all(not(feature = "wrap_help"), feature = "help"))]
    pub(crate) fn wrap(&mut self, _hard_width: usize) {}

    #[cfg(feature = "wrap_help")]
    pub(crate) fn wrap(&mut self, hard_width: usize) {
        let mut new = String::with_capacity(self.0.len());

        let mut last = 0;
        let mut wrapper = crate::output::textwrap::wrap_algorithms::LineWrapper::new(hard_width);
        for content in self.iter_text() {
            // Preserve styling
            let current = content.as_ptr() as usize - self.0.as_str().as_ptr() as usize;
            if last != current {
                new.push_str(&self.0.as_str()[last..current]);
            }
            last = current + content.len();

            for (i, line) in content.split_inclusive('\n').enumerate() {
                if 0 < i {
                    // reset char count on newline, skipping the start as we might have carried
                    // over from a prior block of styled text
                    wrapper.reset();
                }
                let line = crate::output::textwrap::word_separators::find_words_ascii_space(line)
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
                new.extend(wrapper.wrap(line));
            }
        }
        if last != self.0.len() {
            new.push_str(&self.0.as_str()[last..]);
        }
        new = new.trim_end().to_owned();

        self.0 = new;
    }

    #[inline(never)]
    #[cfg(feature = "help")]
    pub(crate) fn display_width(&self) -> usize {
        let mut width = 0;
        for c in self.iter_text() {
            width += crate::output::display_width(c);
        }
        width
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "help")]
    pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.0.is_empty()
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "help")]
    pub(crate) fn as_styled_str(&self) -> &str {
        &self.0
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "color")]
    pub(crate) fn iter_text(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
        anstream::adapter::strip_str(&self.0)
    }

    #[cfg(not(feature = "color"))]
    pub(crate) fn iter_text(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
        [self.0.as_str()].into_iter()
    }

    pub(crate) fn push_styled(&mut self, other: &Self) {
        self.0.push_str(&other.0);
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_to(&self, buffer: &mut dyn std::io::Write) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        ok!(buffer.write_all(self.0.as_bytes()));

        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Default for &'_ StyledStr {
    fn default() -> Self {
        static DEFAULT: StyledStr = StyledStr::new();
        &DEFAULT
    }
}

impl From<String> for StyledStr {
    fn from(name: String) -> Self {
        StyledStr(name)
    }
}

impl From<&'_ String> for StyledStr {
    fn from(name: &'_ String) -> Self {
        let mut styled = StyledStr::new();
        styled.push_str(name);
        styled
    }
}

impl From<&'static str> for StyledStr {
    fn from(name: &'static str) -> Self {
        let mut styled = StyledStr::new();
        styled.push_str(name);
        styled
    }

    Downcast {

    pub(crate) fn unwrap<T>(id: &str, r: Result<T, MatchesError>) -> T {

            Ok(t) => {
                return t;

            Err(err) => err,

        if self.use_stderr() {
            USAGE_CODE
        } else {
            SUCCESS_CODE
        }
    }

    /// Prints the error and exits.

    /// Depending on the error kind, this either prints to `stderr` and exits with a status of `2`
    /// or prints to `stdout` and exits with a status of `0`.
    pub fn exit(&self) -> ! {
        // Swallow broken pipe errors
        let _ = self.print();
        std::process::exit(self.exit_code());
    }

    /// Prints formatted and colored error to `stdout` or `stderr` according to its error kind

    ///         // do_something
    ///     },
    /// };
    /// ```

        let style = self.formatted();

use core::num::NonZeroU16;

use compact_str::CompactString;

use crate::buffer::cell_width::CellWidth;
use crate::style::{Color, Modifier, Style};
use crate::symbols::merge::MergeStrategy;

/// Cell diffing options
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Eq, PartialEq, Hash, Copy)]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
pub enum CellDiffOption {
    #[default]
    /// No special option.
    None,
    /// Skip this cell when diffing.
    ///
    /// This is helpful when it is necessary to prevent the buffer from overwriting a cell that is
    /// covered by something from an escape sequence, such as graphics or links.
    Skip,
    /// Always update this cell when diffing.
    ///
    /// This bypasses the equality check against the previous buffer. Use it when another
    /// renderer may draw over the same area, such as an external image pipeline, so Ratatui can
    /// redraw text there on the next render.
    AlwaysUpdate,
    /// Force a width regardless of the symbol text width.
    ///
    /// Escape sequences will have some computed width that does match what is written to the
    /// screen.
    ForcedWidth(NonZeroU16),
}

/// A buffer cell
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
pub struct Cell {
    /// The string to be drawn in the cell.
    ///
    /// This accepts unicode grapheme clusters which might take up more than one cell.
    ///
    /// This is a [`CompactString`] which is a wrapper around [`String`] that uses a small inline
    /// buffer for short strings.
    ///
    /// See <https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui/pull/601> for more information.
    symbol: Option<CompactString>,

    /// The foreground color of the cell.
    pub fg: Color,

    /// The background color of the cell.
    pub bg: Color,

    /// The underline color of the cell.
    #[cfg(feature = "underline-color")]
    pub underline_color: Color,

    /// The modifier of the cell.
    pub modifier: Modifier,

    /// Special option applied when copying (diffing) the buffer to the screen (or another buffer).
    pub diff_option: CellDiffOption,

    /// Whether the cell should be skipped when copying (diffing) the buffer to the screen.
    ///
    /// Use [`CellDiffOption::Skip`] via [`set_diff_option`](Self::set_diff_option) instead.
    #[deprecated(
        since = "0.30.1",
        note = "use `set_diff_option(CellDiffOption::Skip)` instead"
    )]
    pub skip: bool,
}

impl Cell {
    /// An empty `Cell`
    #[allow(deprecated)]
    pub const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        symbol: None,
        fg: Color::Reset,
        bg: Color::Reset,
        #[cfg(feature = "underline-color")]
        underline_color: Color::Reset,
        modifier: Modifier::empty(),
        diff_option: CellDiffOption::None,
        skip: false,
    };

    /// Creates a new `Cell` with the given symbol.
    ///
    /// This works at compile time and puts the symbol onto the stack. Fails to build when the
    /// symbol doesn't fit onto the stack and requires to be placed on the heap. Use
    /// `Self::default().set_symbol()` in that case. See [`CompactString::const_new`] for more
    /// details on this.
    pub const fn new(symbol: &'static str) -> Self {
        Self {
            symbol: Some(CompactString::const_new(symbol)),
            ..Self::EMPTY
        }
    }

    /// Gets the symbol of the cell.
    ///
    /// If the cell has no symbol, returns a single space character.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn symbol(&self) -> &str {
        self.symbol.as_ref().map_or(" ", |s| s.as_str())
    }

    /// Merges the symbol of the cell with the one already on the cell, using the provided
    /// [`MergeStrategy`].
    ///
    /// Merges [Box Drawing Unicode block] characters to create a single character representing
    /// their combination, useful for [border collapsing]. Currently limited to box drawing
    /// characters, with potential future support for others.
    ///
    /// Merging may not be perfect due to Unicode limitations; some symbol combinations might not
    /// produce a valid character. [`MergeStrategy`] defines how to handle such cases, e.g.,
    /// `Exact` for valid merges only, or `Fuzzy` for close matches.
    ///
    /// If the cell has no symbol set, it will set the symbol to the provided one rather than
    /// merging.
    ///
    /// # Example
    ///
    /// ```
    /// # use ratatui_core::buffer::Cell;
    /// use ratatui_core::symbols::merge::MergeStrategy;
    ///
    /// assert_eq!(
    ///     Cell::new("┘")
    ///         .merge_symbol("┏", MergeStrategy::Exact)
    ///         .symbol(),
    ///     "╆",
    /// );
    ///
    /// assert_eq!(
    ///     Cell::new("╭")
    ///         .merge_symbol("┘", MergeStrategy::Fuzzy)
    ///         .symbol(),
    ///     "┼",
    /// );
    /// ```
    ///
    /// [border collapsing]: https://ratatui.rs/recipes/layout/collapse-borders/
    /// [Box Drawing Unicode block]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box_Drawing
    pub fn merge_symbol(&mut self, symbol: &str, strategy: MergeStrategy) -> &mut Self {
        let merged_symbol = self
            .symbol
            .as_ref()
            .map_or(symbol, |s| strategy.merge(s, symbol));
        self.symbol = Some(CompactString::new(merged_symbol));
        self
    }

    /// Sets the symbol of the cell.
    pub fn set_symbol(&mut self, symbol: &str) -> &mut Self {
        self.symbol = Some(CompactString::new(symbol));
        self
    }

    /// Appends a symbol to the cell.
    ///
    /// This is particularly useful for adding zero-width characters to the cell.
    pub(crate) fn append_symbol(&mut self, symbol: &str) -> &mut Self {
        self.symbol.get_or_insert_default().push_str(symbol);
        self
    }

    /// Sets the symbol of the cell to a single character.

import os, sys, importlib, time
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp'); import probe_new
chars=list("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz;,.'[]/-=")
def mapping(BIN,args,name):
    os.environ["PROBE_BIN"]=BIN; importlib.reload(probe_new)
    s=probe_new.Sess(name,args+" --nokb -c 1 -r 1",80,24)
    out={}
    les=s.cap().splitlines()[6][1:-1].strip()
    for ch in chars:
        b=ch.encode(); hexs=" ".join(f"{c:02x}" for c in b)
        probe_new.run(f"tmux send-keys -t {name} -H {hexs}"); time.sleep(0.06)
        esc6=s.cap(True).splitlines()[6]; plain7=s.cap().splitlines()[7][1:-1].strip()
        reg=("38;5;1" in esc6 or "38;5;2" in esc6)
        trans=plain7 if plain7 else (les[0] if reg else None)
        # if trans is None but reg and plain7 empty, could be space
        if reg and not plain7:
            # determine if green (correct) then bottom space but trans first char; if red, trans is space
            trans=les[0] if "38;5;2" in esc6 else ' '
        out[ch]=trans
        probe_new.run(f"tmux send-keys -t {name} -H 7f"); time.sleep(0.04)
    s.kill(); return out
pairs=[("qwerty","dvorak"),("azerty","colemak"),("qwertz","azerty"),("dvorak","colemakdh"),("colemak","qwertz"),("foo","dvorak")]
for inn,out in pairs:
    a=mapping("/workspace/executable",f"--emu-in {inn} --emu-out {out}","ta")
    b=mapping("/tmp/executable",f"--emu-in {inn} --emu-out {out}","tb")
    print(inn,"->",out,"MATCH" if a==b else "DIFF")
    if a!=b:
        for k in chars:
            if a[k]!=b[k]: print(k,a[k],b[k])

pub struct Layout {
    pub number_row: &'static str,
    pub rows: [&'static str; 3],

    number_row: "`1234567890-=",
    rows: ["qwertyuiop[]", "asdfghjkl;'", "zxcvbnm,./"],

    rows: ["azertyuiop^$", "qsdfghjklmù", "wxcvbn,;:!"],
};
pub const DVORAK: Layout = Layout {
    number_row: "`1234567890[]",

pub const COLEMAKDH: Layout = Layout {

pub fn layout_for(name: &str) -> Layout {
    match name {
        "qwerty" => QWERTY,
        "qwertz" => QWERTZ,
        "azerty" => AZERTY,
        "dvorak" => DVORAK,
        "colemak" => COLEMAK,
        "colemakdh" => COLEMAKDH,
        _ => QWERTY,
    }

pub fn translate(c: char, from: Layout, to: Layout) -> char {
    let from_chars: Vec<char> = from.number_row.chars().chain(from.rows.iter().flat_map(|row| row.chars())).collect();

    pub fn styled_graphemes<S: Into<Style>>(

use crate::layouts::{layout_for, translate, Layout};
use rand::seq::IteratorRandom;
use std::time::Instant;

/// Select one entry at random from the available pool.
///
/// The pool passed to this function is already limited to
/// the requested number of most frequent entries. Picking
/// from an empty pool is not expected to happen in normal
/// use and will panic, as it does when a word list file
/// contains no usable entries at all.
///
/// Each selection is independent, so the same entry can
/// be selected more than once for a single lesson.
fn random_item(available_items: &[String]) -> String {
    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();
    // Choose uniformly from the available entries.
    available_items.iter().choose(&mut rng).unwrap().clone()
}

pub struct Game {
    pub pool: Vec<String>,
    pub top: i32,
    pub combi: i32,
    pub rep: i32,
    pub wpm_needed: i32,
    pub acc_needed: i32,
    pub emu_in: Layout,
    pub emu_out: Layout,
    pub show_ortho: bool,
    pub show_keyboard: bool,
    pub cat: bool,

    pub lesson_number: usize,
    pub target: Vec<char>,
    pub input: Vec<char>,
    pub successes: usize,
    pub failures: usize,
    pub last_wpm: usize,
    pub last_acc: usize,
    pub avg_wpm: usize,
    pub avg_acc: usize,

    correct_strokes: usize,
    total_strokes: usize,
    wpm_values: Vec<usize>,
    acc_values: Vec<usize>,
    started: Option<Instant>,
}

impl Game {
    pub fn new(
        pool: Vec<String>,
        top: i32,
        combi: i32,
        rep: i32,
        wpm_needed: i32,
        acc_needed: i32,
        emu_in_name: &str,
        emu_out_name: &str,
        show_ortho: bool,
        show_keyboard: bool,
        cat: bool,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            pool,
            top,
            combi,
            rep,
            wpm_needed,
            acc_needed,
            emu_in: layout_for(emu_in_name),
            emu_out: layout_for(emu_out_name),
            show_ortho,
            show_keyboard,
            cat,
            lesson_number: 0,
            target: Vec::new(),
            input: Vec::new(),
            successes: 0,
            failures: 0,
            last_wpm: 0,
            last_acc: 0,
            avg_wpm: 0,
            avg_acc: 0,
            correct_strokes: 0,
            total_strokes: 0,
            wpm_values: Vec::new(),
            acc_values: Vec::new(),
            started: None,
        }
    }

    pub fn new_lesson(&mut self) {
        self.lesson_number += 1;
        let usable = self.top.max(0) as usize;
        let choices: Vec<String> = self.pool.iter().take(usable).cloned().collect();
        let mut selected: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..self.combi {
            selected.push(random_item(&choices));
        }
        let mut target = String::new();
        for _ in 0..self.rep {
            for item in &selected {
                target.push_str(item);
                target.push(' ');
            }
        }
        self.target = target.chars().collect();
        self.input.clear();
        self.correct_strokes = 0;
        self.total_strokes = 0;
        self.started = None;
    }

    fn finish_lesson_if_complete(&mut self) {
        if self.input != self.target {
            return;
        }
        let elapsed = self.started.map(|start| start.elapsed()).unwrap_or_default();
